I will keep things steady and practical this year. In Quzhou County, the safest way for me to farm is still the wheat-maize rotation. I know this system, it fits our climate and water conditions, and it gives me grain from two seasons on the same land. At my age, I do not want to gamble on a crop that needs more market chasing or more delicate management. I will plant winter wheat on all my land, then after harvest I will plant summer maize right away. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, better disease resistance, and more reliable yield. For fertilizer, I will not push too hard, because too much nitrogen can lodge the crop and waste money, but I will still feed enough to protect yield. Water is always important here, so I will irrigate wheat more than maize. For tillage, I will plough before wheat to prepare the soil well, and after wheat I will use rotary tillage for fast maize planting. I will keep pesticide use moderate and only aim to control the main diseases, insects, and weeds so the crop stays clean without overspending.
